title: Article 117 — Special provisions as to financial Bills

content.overview: Article 117 provides special rules for financial Bills: a Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters in Article 110(1) (Money Bill subjects) shall not be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of the President, and a Bill making such provision shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. A Bill which, if enacted, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India shall not be passed by either House unless the President has recommended consideration of the Bill to that House. These rules do not apply to Bills for reduction or abolition of tax (and certain other limited cases).
content.glance: Financial Bills involving Art 110 matters: Presidential recommendation; not introducible in RS. Bills involving Consolidated Fund expenditure: Presidential recommendation for consideration. Tax reduction/abolition exception.
content.study:
Article 117 distinguishes:

(1) Bills/amendments making provision for Money Bill subjects (Art 110(1)): require Presidential recommendation for introduction/movement; cannot be introduced in the Council of States.

(2) Bills involving expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India: shall not be passed by either House unless the President has recommended to that House the consideration of the Bill.

(3) Exceptions include Bills for the reduction or abolition of any tax.

Distinguish from pure Money Bills (Art 109–110 special procedure) and ordinary Bills.

Examination: recommendation requirements; RS introduction bar for Art 110-matter Bills; expenditure Bills; tax reduction exception.

sections.heading: Special rules
sections.body:
1. Art 110-matter provision in a Bill/amendment → Presidential recommendation; not introducible in RS.
2. Bill involving Consolidated Fund expenditure → Presidential recommendation for consideration before passage.
3. Exception: reduction or abolition of any tax (and related limited cases).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Article 117.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 117 requires the President’s recommendation for introduction or movement of a Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters in Article 110(1), and such a Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. A Bill that would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India shall not be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration to that House. These restrictions do not apply to a Bill for the reduction or abolition of any tax.
